newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ICI to spend A$16.5 mln on upgrade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ICI to spend A$16.5 mln on upgrade.

text.p: British-owned chemicals group ICI Australia Ltd said on Wednesday it planned a A$16.5 million upgrade of its alkathene plant at Botany on the southern shores of Sydney.
"The investment will increase the plant's capacity to produce extruded product by 23,000 tonnes per annum," ICI said.
The upgrade would start immediately and was scheduled for completion by late 1997.

"The major impact will be our increased ability to satisfy specific customer requirements through greater scope for blending and tailoring of plastic resin properties," ICI divisional manager Greg Witcombe said in a statement.

"The upgrade will also serve to streamline the manufacturing process which will result in some productivity efficiencies. As well, the installation of new state-of-the-art extrusion technology will improve plant reliability and product consistency," he said.
ICI was looking to supply growth areas for plastic resins both in Australia and Asia, he said.
Alkathene is used in a wide range of general packaging applications including plastic film and milk carton linings.
ICI shares were up ten cents at A$12.65 at 11.00 a.m. (2400 GMT).
The company is 62.4 percent owned by Imperial Chemical Industries Ltd.
